claim: ELYS is encoded by AHCTF1
source: The nucleoporin (NUP) ELYS, encoded by AHCTF1, is a large multifunctional protein with essential roles in nuclear pore assembly and mitosis.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of the protein

claim: ELYS has essential roles in nuclear pore assembly and mitosis
source: The nucleoporin (NUP) ELYS, encoded by AHCTF1, is a large multifunctional protein with essential roles in nuclear pore assembly and mitosis.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript

claim: Reducing ahctf1 gene dosage by 50% markedly decreases liver volume in krasG12V-expressing zebrafish
source: we show that reducing ahctf1 gene dosage by 50% markedly decreases liver volume, while non-hyperplastic tissues are unaffected.
evidence: Directly stated in abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1

claim: Non-hyperplastic tissues are unaffected by ahctf1 heterozygosity
source: we show that reducing ahctf1 gene dosage by 50% markedly decreases liver volume, while non-hyperplastic tissues are unaffected.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by data showing normal development in control larvae

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs nuclear pore formation in the context of cancer
source: We demonstrate that in the context of cancer, ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs nuclear pore formation, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation, leading to DNA damage and activation of a Tp53-dependent transcriptional programme that induces cell death and cell cycle arrest.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by mAb414 staining data in Figure 2

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs mitotic spindle assembly in the context of cancer
source: We demonstrate that in the context of cancer, ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs nuclear pore formation, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation, leading to DNA damage and activation of a Tp53-dependent transcriptional programme that induces cell death and cell cycle arrest.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by α-tubulin staining data in Figure 3

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs chromosome segregation in the context of cancer
source: We demonstrate that in the context of cancer, ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs nuclear pore formation, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation, leading to DNA damage and activation of a Tp53-dependent transcriptional programme that induces cell death and cell cycle arrest.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by mitotic analysis in Figure 3

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity leads to DNA damage in krasG12V-expressing hepatocytes
source: We demonstrate that in the context of cancer, ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs nuclear pore formation, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation, leading to DNA damage and activation of a Tp53-dependent transcriptional programme that induces cell death and cell cycle arrest.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by γ-H2AX staining in Figure 4

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity activates a Tp53-dependent transcriptional programme
source: We demonstrate that in the context of cancer, ahctf1 heterozygosity impairs nuclear pore formation, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation, leading to DNA damage and activation of a Tp53-dependent transcriptional programme that induces cell death and cell cycle arrest.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by Tp53 protein accumulation and target gene expression in Figures 4-6

claim: Heterozygous expression of both ahctf1 and ranbp2 completely blocks krasG12V-driven hepatocyte hyperplasia
source: Heterozygous expression of both ahctf1 and ranbp2 (encoding a second nucleoporin), or treatment of heterozygous ahctf1 larvae with the nucleocytoplasmic transport inhibitor, Selinexor, completely blocks krasG12V-driven hepatocyte hyperplasia.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by liver volume measurements in Figure 7

claim: Treatment of heterozygous ahctf1 larvae with Selinexor completely blocks krasG12V-driven hepatocyte hyperplasia
source: Heterozygous expression of both ahctf1 and ranbp2 (encoding a second nucleoporin), or treatment of heterozygous ahctf1 larvae with the nucleocytoplasmic transport inhibitor, Selinexor, completely blocks krasG12V-driven hepatocyte hyperplasia.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by liver volume measurements in Figure 7

claim: High expression of NUP107-160 subcomplex components is positively correlated with worse overall survival in HCC patients
source: Gene expression analysis of patient samples in the liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) dataset in The Cancer Genome Atlas shows that high expression of one or more of the transcripts encoding the 10 components of the NUP107–160 subcomplex, which includes AHCTF1, is positively correlated with worse overall survival.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by TCGA analysis in Figure 8

claim: Homozygous inheritance of ahctf1ti262 mutation disrupted nuclear pore formation in zebrafish
source: We became interested in AHCTF1 when we and others showed that homozygous inheritance of an ENU-induced nonsense mutation in the zebrafish ahctf1 gene (ahctf1ti262) (de Jong-Curtain et al., 2009; Davuluri et al., 2008) disrupted nuclear pore formation and caused catastrophic levels of cell death in the intestinal epithelium and other highly proliferative cell compartments during zebrafish development (de Jong-Curtain et al., 2009; Davuluri et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with citations to previous work

claim: Homozygous ahctf1ti262 mutation caused catastrophic levels of cell death in highly proliferative cell compartments during zebrafish development
source: We became interested in AHCTF1 when we and others showed that homozygous inheritance of an ENU-induced nonsense mutation in the zebrafish ahctf1 gene (ahctf1ti262) (de Jong-Curtain et al., 2009; Davuluri et al., 2008) disrupted nuclear pore formation and caused catastrophic levels of cell death in the intestinal epithelium and other highly proliferative cell compartments during zebrafish development (de Jong-Curtain et al., 2009; Davuluri et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with citations to previous work

claim: Cells in relatively quiescent tissues survived and remained healthy with homozygous ahctf1ti262 mutation
source: Meanwhile, cells in relatively quiescent tissues survived and remained healthy.
evidence: Stated with reference to previous findings

claim: ELYS was first discovered in mice
source: AHCTF1 encodes ELYS, a 252-kDa multidomain nucleoporin (NUP) that was first discovered in mice where it was shown to be required for the proliferation and survival of inner mass cells during embryonic development (Okita et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated with citation to Okita et al., 2004

claim: ELYS is required for the proliferation and survival of inner mass cells during embryonic development in mice
source: AHCTF1 encodes ELYS, a 252-kDa multidomain nucleoporin (NUP) that was first discovered in mice where it was shown to be required for the proliferation and survival of inner mass cells during embryonic development (Okita et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated with citation to Okita et al., 2004

claim: ELYS is one of 10 components of the NUP107-160 subunit of nuclear pore complexes
source: ELYS is one of 10 components of the large NUP107–160 subunit of nuclear pore complexes (NPCs).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claim: Nuclear pore complexes comprise approximately 34 different NUPs in octameric array
source: These huge (110 MDa) multi-subunit complexes comprise approximately 34 different NUPs in octameric array (Beck and Hurt, 2017; Petrovic et al., 2022), forming cylindrical channels in the nuclear envelope that regulate nucleocytoplasmic transport and intracellular localisation of large (>40 kDa) molecules.
evidence: Stated with citations to Beck and Hurt, 2017; Petrovic et al., 2022

claim: ELYS is indispensable for NPC reassembly after mitosis
source: ELYS is also indispensable for NPC reassembly after mitosis (Rasala et al., 2006; Gillespie et al., 2007; Franz et al., 2007) and carries out a broad range of activities during the cell cycle, including chromatin decompaction, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation (Gillespie et al., 2007; Kuhn et al., 2019; Güttinger et al., 2009; Chatel and Fahrenkrog, 2011; Mishra et al., 2010; Yokoyama et al., 2014; Kobayashi et al., 2019; Rasala et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with multiple citations

claim: ELYS carries out activities including chromatin decompaction, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation during the cell cycle
source: ELYS is also indispensable for NPC reassembly after mitosis (Rasala et al., 2006; Gillespie et al., 2007; Franz et al., 2007) and carries out a broad range of activities during the cell cycle, including chromatin decompaction, mitotic spindle assembly, and chromosome segregation (Gillespie et al., 2007; Kuhn et al., 2019; Güttinger et al., 2009; Chatel and Fahrenkrog, 2011; Mishra et al., 2010; Yokoyama et al., 2014; Kobayashi et al., 2019; Rasala et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with multiple citations

claim: The RAS/RAF/MAPK signalling pathway is almost always hyperactivated in human HCC
source: We chose this model of HCC because the RAS/RAF/MAPK signalling pathway is almost always hyperactivated in human HCC (Calvisi et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated with citation to Calvisi et al., 2006

claim: Dox treatment between 2 and 7 dpf induces EGFP-krasG12V expression in developing zebrafish livers
source: In our larval model, on a wildtype (WT) ahctf1 background, we induced the expression of a single EGFP-krasG12V transgene, denoted TO(krasG12V)T/+ in developing livers by treating with dox between 2 and 7 days post-fertilisation (dpf) (Figure 1a, b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1a protocol diagram

claim: krasG12V expression causes hepatocyte hyperplasia and a 4-fold increase in liver volume
source: This led to the accumulation of a constitutively active, EGFP-tagged, potently oncogenic form of Kras (KrasG12V) specifically in hepatocytes, causing hepatocyte hyperplasia and a substantial increase (4-fold) in liver volume (Figure 1c, d).
evidence: Stated in text and quantified in Figure 1d

claim: More than 6000 genes were significantly upregulated in dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers compared to WT livers
source: We detected more than 6000 significantly upregulated genes in dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers compared WT livers, and a further 6000+ genes were significantly downregulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, b

claim: More than 6000 genes were significantly downregulated in dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers compared to WT livers
source: We detected more than 6000 significantly upregulated genes in dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers compared WT livers, and a further 6000+ genes were significantly downregulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, b

claim: There is a positive correlation between differential gene expression in dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ versus WT livers and the HCC (LIHC) dataset from TCGA
source: Gene set enrichment analysis identified a positive correlation between the differential gene expression data from the dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ versus WT livers and the differential gene expression data obtained from the HCC (LIHC) and healthy liver subsets available in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c

claim: There is a positive correlation between DEGs from dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ versus WT livers and a small HCC expression signature based on four patient samples carrying KRAS G12 or KRAS G13 mutations
source: We also found a positive correlation between the diffentially expressed genes (DEGs) from the dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ versus WT livers and a small HCC expression signature based on four patient samples carrying KRAS G12 or KRAS G13 mutations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1d

claim: Upregulated genes in dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers are significantly enriched in KEGG pathways associated with highly proliferative cancers
source: Of the upregulated genes, many were significantly enriched in KEGG pathways associated with highly proliferative cancers, including DNA replication, cell cycle regulation, and DNA damage repair (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1e

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity produces a 57% reduction in ahctf1 mRNA expression in larvae at 7 dpf
source: This produced a 57% reduction in ahctf1 mRNA expression in ahctf1+/− larvae at 7 dpf, compared to larvae expressing WT ahctf1 (Figure 1b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1b

claim: The nonsense mutation in ahctf1ti262 triggers nonsense mediated decay of mRNA rather than translation of a truncated protein
source: This is consistent with the nonsense mutation in ahctf1ti262 triggering nonsense mediated decay of mRNA transcribed from the affected allele, rather than it being translated and expressed as a truncated Elys protein.
evidence: Inferred from the mRNA reduction data

claim: Heterozygous ahctf1ti262 zebrafish develop normally
source: On this background, heterozygous (HET) ahctf1ti262 zebrafish develop normally (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a), reach sexual maturity, and exhibit a normal lifespan, as do HET ahctf1 mice (Okita et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2a, with citation to mouse data

claim: Heterozygous ahctf1 mice exhibit a normal lifespan
source: On this background, heterozygous (HET) ahctf1ti262 zebrafish develop normally (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a), reach sexual maturity, and exhibit a normal lifespan, as do HET ahctf1 mice (Okita et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated with citation to Okita et al., 2004

claim: Mean liver volume in control 2-CLiP larvae at 7 dpf was 1.95 × 10^6 ± 4.99 × 10^4 μm³
source: Mean liver volume in control 2-CLiP larvae at 7 dpf was 1.95 × 106 ± 4.99 × 104 μm3 and was unaffected by ahctf1 genotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a, b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b

claim: Liver volume in control 2-CLiP larvae is unaffected by ahctf1 genotype
source: Mean liver volume in control 2-CLiP larvae at 7 dpf was 1.95 × 106 ± 4.99 × 104 μm3 and was unaffected by ahctf1 genotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a, b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b

claim: Dox-induced krasG12V expression produced a 4-fold increase in liver volume to 7.97 × 10^6 ± 1.21 × 10^5 μm³
source: Dox-induced expression of oncogenic KrasG12V in the TO(krasG12V)T/+ model, produced a striking (4-fold) increase in liver volume (7.97 × 106 ± 1.21 × 105 μm3) over the 5 days of dox treatment (Figure 1c, d).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1d

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity reduced liver volume to 5.92 × 10^6 ± 8.83 × 10^4 µm³ in krasG12V-expressing larvae
source: Remarkably, liver volume was pared back to 5.92 × 106 ± 8.83 × 104 µm3 in ahctf1 HETS, equating to a 35% reduction in excess liver volume.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1d

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity produces a 35% reduction in excess liver volume in krasG12V-expressing larvae
source: Remarkably, liver volume was pared back to 5.92 × 106 ± 8.83 × 104 µm3 in ahctf1 HETS, equating to a 35% reduction in excess liver volume.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1d

claim: Dox induction of krasG12V expression produced a 9-fold increase in liver mass as a percentage of total body mass in male zebrafish expressing WT ahctf1
source: Compared to vehicle-treated animals, we found that dox induction of krasG12V expression produced a robust (9-fold) increase in liver mass expressed as a percentage of total body mass of male zebrafish expressing WT ahctf1.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1e

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity reduced liver-to-body mass ratio by 28% in adult male krasG12V-expressing zebrafish
source: This ratio was reduced by 28% in ahctf1 HETS and we obtained similar results with females (Figure 1e).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1e

claim: Dox-treated ahctf1+/+; TO(krasG12V)T/+ male livers exhibited severely disrupted architecture and loss of hepatocyte organisation
source: In contrast, dox-treated ahctf1+/+; TO(krasG12V)T/+-expressing male livers exhibited severely disrupted architecture, and a general loss of hepatocyte organisation (Figure 1f, bottom left).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1f

claim: Hepatocytes in dox-treated ahctf1+/+; TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers were generally poorly differentiated and some exhibited pyknotic nuclei, condensed nucleoli, and vacuolation
source: Hepatocytes were generally poorly differentiated and some exhibited features such as pyknotic nuclei, condensed nucleoli, and vacuolation (Figure 1f, bottom left).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1f

claim: Sections of krasG12V-expressing livers from ahctf1 heterozygotes showed hepatocytes with improved nuclear integrity and less vacuolation
source: Sections of krasG12V-expressing livers from ahctf1 HETS showed hepatocytes with improved nuclear integrity and less vacuolation (Figure 1f, bottom right).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1f

claim: Dox treatment markedly increased the abundance of EGFP-KrasG12V protein in TO(krasG12V)T/+ zebrafish larvae
source: Dox treatment markedly increased the abundance of the EGFP-KrasG12V protein in lysates of TO(krasG12V)T/+ zebrafish larvae compared to vehicle-treated larvae (Figure 1g), and this was unaffected by ahctf1 genotype.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1g

claim: EGFP-KrasG12V protein abundance is unaffected by ahctf1 genotype
source: Dox treatment markedly increased the abundance of the EGFP-KrasG12V protein in lysates of TO(krasG12V)T/+ zebrafish larvae compared to vehicle-treated larvae (Figure 1g), and this was unaffected by ahctf1 genotype.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1g

claim: The intensity of activated EGFP-KrasG12V-GTP signals was not affected by ahctf1 genotype
source: In vehicle-treated zebrafish larvae, signals corresponding to GTP-bound endogenous Ras proteins were weak, whereas lysates from dox-treated larvae gave robust signals corresponding to activated EGFP-KrasG12V proteins. The intensity of these signals was not affected by ahctf1 genotype (Figure 1h).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1h

claim: The impact of heterozygous ahctf1 mutation on hepatocyte growth, proliferation, and survival did not occur by interfering with the production of GTP-bound Ras proteins
source: Thus, the impact of heterozygous ahctf1 mutation on the growth, proliferation, and survival of TO(krasG12V)T/+ expressing hepatocytes did not occur by directly or indirectly interfering with the production of GTP-bound Ras proteins.
evidence: Inferred from the Ras-GTP pull-down data showing no difference

claim: Fluorescence intensity of mAb414 staining was markedly increased in dox-treated TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes
source: In dox-treated larvae harbouring the TO(krasG12V)T/+ transgene, fluorescence intensity was markedly increased (Figure 2a, third column) and there was an increase in the ratio of nuclear:cytoplasmic staining (Figure 2b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2a, b

claim: Fluorescence intensity at the nuclear rim was diminished in ahctf1 heterozygotes with krasG12V expression
source: By comparison, fluorescence intensity at the nuclear rim was diminished in ahctf1 HETS, concomitant with the appearance of fluorescent puncta in the cytoplasm (Figure 2a, fourth column; arrows) and a significant reduction in the ratio of nuclear:cytoplasmic fluorescence intensity (Figure 2b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2a, b

claim: Fluorescent puncta appeared in the cytoplasm of ahctf1 heterozygous hepatocytes expressing krasG12V
source: By comparison, fluorescence intensity at the nuclear rim was diminished in ahctf1 HETS, concomitant with the appearance of fluorescent puncta in the cytoplasm (Figure 2a, fourth column; arrows) and a significant reduction in the ratio of nuclear:cytoplasmic fluorescence intensity (Figure 2b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2a

claim: Induced krasG12V expression resulted in 59% more NPCs at the nuclear surface of hyperplastic hepatocytes
source: The induced expression of the krasG12V transgene in the presence of WT ahctf1 resulted in 59% more fluorescent puncta/NPCs at the nuclear surface of hyperplastic hepatocytes (Figure 2c, d; third column).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2c, d

claim: NPC density was reduced by 21% in ahctf1 heterozygotes expressing krasG12V
source: These signals were reduced by 21% in ahctf1 HETS (Figure 2c, d; fourth column).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2c, d

claim: Induced krasG12V expression produced a 28% increase in nuclear volume compared to non-krasG12V-expressing cells
source: Induced krasG12V expression also produced a 28% increase in nuclear volume compared to non-krasG12V-expressing cells (Figure 2e), and this increase in size was reduced to 13% in ahctf1 HETS.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2e

claim: The increase in nuclear volume with krasG12V expression was reduced to 13% in ahctf1 heterozygotes
source: Induced krasG12V expression also produced a 28% increase in nuclear volume compared to non-krasG12V-expressing cells (Figure 2e), and this increase in size was reduced to 13% in ahctf1 HETS.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 2e

claim: Hyperplastic hepatocytes expressing krasG12V require highly efficient rates of nucleocytoplasmic transport to support their rapid proliferation
source: We infer from these data that hyperplastic hepatocytes expressing the krasG12V oncogene require highly efficient rates of nucleocytoplasmic transport to support their rapid proliferation, which they fulfil by increasing NPC density and the size of their nuclei.
evidence: Inferred from the NPC density and nuclear volume data

claim: Hyperplastic hepatocytes fulfill their need for efficient nucleocytoplasmic transport by increasing NPC density and nuclear size
source: We infer from these data that hyperplastic hepatocytes expressing the krasG12V oncogene require highly efficient rates of nucleocytoplasmic transport to support their rapid proliferation, which they fulfil by increasing NPC density and the size of their nuclei.
evidence: Inferred from the NPC density and nuclear volume data

claim: This adaptation required a full complement of ahctf1 expression
source: This adaptation required a full complement of ahctf1 expression, suggesting non-oncogene addiction to ahctf1.
evidence: Inferred from the requirement for WT ahctf1 to achieve full NPC density increase

claim: Metaphase cells in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers exhibited normal bipolar spindle formation followed by complete chromosome segregation during anaphase
source: Metaphase cells in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers exhibited normal bipolar spindle formation followed by complete chromosome segregation during anaphase (Figure 3a).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 3a

claim: Metaphase cells in ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes displayed abnormal multipolar spindles and misaligned chromosomes
source: In contrast, metaphase cells in ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes displayed abnormal multipolar spindles and misaligned chromosomes (Figure 3b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 3b

claim: Proper chromosome segregation was disrupted with multiple anaphase bridges formed in ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes
source: Proper chromosome segregation was disrupted with multiple anaphase bridges formed.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 3b

claim: The number of cells observed at different mitotic stages was similar in ahctf1+/+ and ahctf1+/−
source: While the number of cells observed at different mitotic stages was similar in ahctf1+/+ and ahctf1+/− (Figure 3c), mitotic abnormalities were observed in 50% of ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes during metaphase and anaphase but not at all in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes (Figure 3d).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 3c

claim: Mitotic abnormalities were observed in 50% of ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes during metaphase and anaphase
source: While the number of cells observed at different mitotic stages was similar in ahctf1+/+ and ahctf1+/− (Figure 3c), mitotic abnormalities were observed in 50% of ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes during metaphase and anaphase but not at all in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes (Figure 3d).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 3d

claim: No mitotic abnormalities were observed in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes
source: While the number of cells observed at different mitotic stages was similar in ahctf1+/+ and ahctf1+/− (Figure 3c), mitotic abnormalities were observed in 50% of ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes during metaphase and anaphase but not at all in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocytes (Figure 3d).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 3d

claim: 1% of ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocyte nuclei were positive for γ-H2AX
source: We found that 1% of ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocyte nuclei were positive for γ-H2AX (Figure 4a, c), compared to 6% in the nuclei of ahctf1 HETS (Figure 4b, c).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 4c

claim: 6% of ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocyte nuclei were positive for γ-H2AX
source: We found that 1% of ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ hepatocyte nuclei were positive for γ-H2AX (Figure 4a, c), compared to 6% in the nuclei of ahctf1 HETS (Figure 4b, c).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 4c

claim: A weak Tp53 signal was detected in extracts of dox-treated ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers
source: However, we detected a weak Tp53 signal in extracts of dox-treated ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers, consistent with induced krasG12V expression causing mild cellular stress.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 4d, e

claim: Heterozygous ahctf1 livers showed a >3.5-fold increase in Tp53 signal intensity
source: This low level of stress was amplified significantly in heterozygous ahctf1 livers, where we obtained a strong (>3.5-fold) increase in the intensity of the Tp53 signal (Figure 4e), which correlated well with the higher density of γ-H2AX staining.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 4e

claim: Abrogating Tp53 function in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ larvae increased liver volume by 50%
source: Abrogating Tp53 function by homozygous expression of this allele (denoted tp53m/m) in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ larvae increased liver volume by 50%, to 12.5 × 106 ± 1.10 × 105 μm3, compared to livers on a WT (tp53+/+) background (Figure 4f, g), demonstrating that Tp53 function normally places great restraint on the growth of TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers in this model.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 4f, g

claim: Tp53 function normally places great restraint on the growth of TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers
source: Abrogating Tp53 function by homozygous expression of this allele (denoted tp53m/m) in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ larvae increased liver volume by 50%, to 12.5 × 106 ± 1.10 × 105 μm3, compared to livers on a WT (tp53+/+) background (Figure 4f, g), demonstrating that Tp53 function normally places great restraint on the growth of TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers in this model.
evidence: Inferred from the 50% increase in liver volume when Tp53 is abrogated

claim: ahctf1 heterozygosity combined with loss of Tp53 function produced a 50% increase in liver volume compared to ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers on a WT Tp53 background
source: ahctf1 heterozygosity combined with loss of Tp53 function also produced an increase in liver volume by 50% compared to ahctf1+/−;TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers on a WT Tp53 background.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 4g

claim: Heterozygous ahctf1 still achieved a reduction in liver volume on a Tp53 mutant background, albeit significantly less than in the presence of WT Tp53
source: Comparing the volume of ahctf1 HET livers and WT ahctf1 livers on a Tp53 mutant background, showed that heterozygous ahctf1 still achieved a reduction in liver volume, albeit significantly less than in the presence of WT Tp53.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 4g

claim: The abundance of Annexin 5 fluorescent puncta was 1.5 puncta per 10^-5 μm³ in ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ larvae
source: The abundance of Annexin 5 fluorescent puncta was 1.5 puncta per 10−5 μm3 in the livers of WT Tp53, ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ larvae and this value increased by 3.5-fold (5.2 puncta per 10−5 μm3) on a heterozygous ahctf1 background (Figure 5a, left two columns, Figure 5b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 5b

claim: Annexin 5 puncta increased by 3.5-fold to 5.2 puncta per 10^-5 μm³ on a heterozygous ahctf1 background
source: The abundance of Annexin 5 fluorescent puncta was 1.5 puncta per 10−5 μm3 in the livers of WT Tp53, ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ larvae and this value increased by 3.5-fold (5.2 puncta per 10−5 μm3) on a heterozygous ahctf1 background (Figure 5a, left two columns, Figure 5b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 5b

claim: Annexin 5 puncta were relatively sparse (0.13 puncta per 10^-5 μm³) in Tp53-deficient livers on a ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ background
source: Compared to those expressing WT Tp53 (1.5 puncta per 10−5 μm3), Annexin 5 puncta were relatively sparse (0.13 puncta per 10−5 μm3) in Tp53-deficient livers on a ahctf1+/+;TO(krasG12V)T/+ background.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5b

claim: The death of hepatocytes in ahctf1 WT, TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers is normally kept in check by Tp53
source: This robust (11.3-fold) reduction in the density of Annexin 5 foci indicates that the death of hepatocytes in ahctf1 WT, TO(krasG12V)T/+ livers is normally kept in check by Tp53 (Figure 5a, b).
evidence: Inferred from the 11.3-fold reduction in Annexin 5 foci when Tp53 is deficient

claim: The density of Annexin 5 puncta on a tp53m/m background was 2.3 puncta per 10^-5 μm³ in ahctf1 heterozygotes
source: Turning to ahctf1 HETS, the density of Annexin 5 puncta on a tp53m/m background was 2.3 puncta per 10−5 μm3, less than half the number of puncta (5.2 per 10−5 μm3) on a WT Tp53 background (Figure 5a, b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 5b

claim: The number of hepatocytes undergoing apoptosis on a Tp53-deficient background remained higher in heterozygous ahctf1 larvae compared to ahctf1 WT larvae
